newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines says rice and corn stocks rise.
newsitem.headline: Philippines says rice and corn stocks rise.

text.p: Philippine rice stocks increased by 26 percent to 1.739 million tonnes as of January 3 this year against the 1.374 million tonnes a year ago, the state-run National Food Authority (NFA) said.
NFA also said the country's corn stocks grew 24.5 percent to 340,400 tonnes from the year-ago 273,000 tonnes.

"The country's total rice inventory as of January 3 is good for 79 days based on the average requirement of 22,000 tonnes per day," NFA director for public affairs Vicente Racho told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Racho also said the country's corn stocks as of January 3 could only sustain requirements of livestock farmers for 23 days based on daily consumption of 14,600 tonnes.

Agriculture Secretary Salvador Escudero said earlier he expected the country to import between 300,000 and 500,000 tonnes of rice and up to 500,000 tonnes of corn this year due to a projected shortfall in the second half, which is a traditionally lean time for local rice and corn harvests.
